title: Grade 2 Science — Mon, May 18
description: Plants Around Us — Day 1 of 5: Parts of a plant
subject: science

questions.question: Which part of the plant is under the ground?
questions.explanation: Roots grow underground. They hold the plant in the soil and soak up water and minerals.

questions.question: What does the leaf do for the plant?
questions.explanation: Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight, water, and air. This process is called photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which part of the plant holds it up straight?
questions.explanation: The stem holds the plant upright and carries water from the roots up to the leaves.

questions.question: Where do seeds come from?
questions.explanation: Seeds are found inside fruits. Flowers turn into fruits, and fruits contain seeds.

questions.question: A mango tree is a:
questions.explanation: A mango tree is a tall plant with a thick, hard stem — it is a tree. Trees live for many years.

questions.question: Which of these is a creeper?
questions.explanation: Pumpkin is a creeper — it grows along the ground. Other examples: watermelon, sweet potato vine.

questions.question: What does a plant need to grow?
questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight, water, air, and soil (for minerals) to grow and make food.

questions.question: The rose plant is a:
questions.explanation: Rose is a shrub — it is a medium-sized plant with many branches from near the base. Other shrubs: hibiscus, mehendi.

questions.question: Which part of the plant makes new plants?
questions.explanation: Seeds grow into new plants. When a seed is planted in soil and watered, it sprouts and becomes a new plant.

questions.question: The grass in a garden is a:
questions.explanation: Grass is an herb — a small, soft plant with a thin green stem. Other herbs: tulsi, mint, spinach.

questions.question: Which of these is a part of a plant?
questions.explanation: Root, stem, leaf, flower, and fruit are parts of a plant. Tail, wing, and paw are animal body parts.

questions.question: What colour are most leaves?
questions.explanation: Most leaves are green because they contain a green substance called chlorophyll, which helps them make food.

questions.question: Which plant part drinks water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil. The water then travels up through the stem to the leaves.

questions.question: A cactus lives in a:
questions.explanation: Cactus is a desert plant. It can store water in its thick stem and survive in very dry, hot places.

questions.question: Which part of the plant do we use to make salad from a lettuce plant?
questions.explanation: Lettuce leaves are used in salad. We eat different parts of different plants — roots (carrot), stem (sugarcane), leaf (spinach).
